title: Mock 7 · Final Boss
blurb: Caselets on a rights-plus-bonus sequence and fund performance attribution, two-stage DCF, SOTP, the 2024-25 RA amendments and indicator maths.

questions.q: To protect the independence of research at a firm that also does investment banking, the RA Regulations require that:
options: Analysts report to the head of investment banking for faster deal coordination
Analysts receive a fixed share of fees from IPOs they cover
Analyst compensation is not linked to any specific merchant banking, investment banking or brokerage transaction
Analysts may participate in deal pitches if they disclose it later
questions.explanation: Analysts must not be supervised by investment-banking staff, and their compensation must not be tied to specific merchant/investment banking or brokerage transactions; it is reviewed by a body excluding those divisions.
hints: Supervision by investment banking staff is prohibited.
Participating in solicitation compromises independence; later disclosure does not cure it.

questions.q: A stock trades at ₹1,000 in the cash market while its one-month future trades at ₹1,030, well above fair value. A trader buys the stock in the cash market and sells the future, holding both to expiry. This is:
options: A hedge by a long-term investor against a price rise
questions.explanation: Buying cash and selling overpriced futures locks in the price gap (net of carry costs) regardless of direction - classic cash-and-carry arbitrage.
hints: The positions offset each other, so it is not a naked view.
A hedge reduces an existing exposure; here the trader creates offsetting positions to lock in a gap.
Pledging is using shares as loan collateral.

questions.q: A company has market cap ₹10,000 crore, debt ₹3,000 crore, preference capital ₹500 crore, minority interest ₹700 crore and cash ₹1,200 crore. Its enterprise value is:
hints: This adds cash instead of subtracting it.
This omits preference capital and minority interest.

questions.q: India's current account deficit widens sharply while foreign portfolio investors pull money out of Indian equities. Other things equal, the most likely effect is:
options: The rupee appreciates against the dollar
Imported crude becomes cheaper in rupee terms
The rupee tends to depreciate against the dollar
questions.explanation: A wider CAD increases demand for dollars and FPI outflows reduce dollar supply; both put depreciation pressure on the rupee.
hints: Both forces push the rupee down, not up.
A weaker rupee makes imports costlier.
If RBI intervenes it would sell dollars, reducing reserves.

questions.q: Which pairing of industry and key performance indicator is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Same-store sales growth is a retail metric. Banks are tracked on NIM, credit growth, CASA, GNPA/NNPA and capital adequacy.
hints: Correct - this is the wrong pairing.

questions.q: Consider the BCG matrix statements: (I) Cash Cows often fund investment in Question Marks. (II) Dogs have high market share in low-growth markets. (III) Stars usually need substantial investment to sustain their growth. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Cash Cows generate surplus cash that funds Question Marks (I true). Dogs have LOW share in low-growth markets (II false). Stars need heavy investment to keep up with market growth (III true).

questions.q: In ESG analysis, which of the following is primarily a 'Social' factor?
options: Workplace safety record and employee attrition
Water consumption per unit of output
questions.explanation: Social factors cover employees, safety, community, customers and supply-chain labour practices. Emissions and water are Environmental; board independence is Governance.

questions.q: A company's return on assets (PAT / total assets) is 6% and its debt-equity ratio is 1.5. Assuming total assets = debt + equity, its ROE is:
questions.explanation: Equity multiplier = assets/equity = (D + E)/E = 1 + 1.5 = 2.5. ROE = ROA x equity multiplier = 6% x 2.5 = 15%.
hints: This multiplies ROA by D/E (1.5) instead of the equity multiplier.

questions.q: A profitable company whose return on assets exceeds its after-tax cost of debt borrows money to buy back shares. All else equal, what happens to its ROE and debt-equity ratio?
questions.explanation: Replacing equity with cheaper debt increases financial leverage: equity shrinks and debt rises, so D/E rises; since returns on assets exceed the after-tax cost of debt, ROE also rises (the DuPont equity multiplier effect).
hints: Debt rises and equity falls, so D/E cannot fall.
A higher equity multiplier changes ROE.
ROE falls only if the cost of debt exceeds the return on assets.

questions.q: FCFF is forecast at ₹110 crore in year 1 and ₹121 crore in year 2, then grows at 5% forever. With a WACC of 12%, the enterprise value today is approximately:
hints: This discounts the terminal value by three years instead of two.
This forgets to grow year-2 FCFF by 5% in the terminal value.
This omits the terminal value entirely.

questions.q: For valuing a bank or NBFC, the most commonly used relative-valuation multiple is:
questions.explanation: For lenders, debt is raw material rather than financing, so EV-based multiples are not meaningful; P/B (often adjusted for NPAs) together with ROE is the standard approach.
hints: EV and EBITDA are not meaningful for banks.
Same problem - EV is not meaningful for lenders.
PEG can be used, but P/B is the standard for financials.

questions.q: A holding company's core business is valued at ₹5,000 crore (EV). It also owns a listed stake worth ₹2,000 crore at market, to which the analyst applies a 20% holding-company discount. Net debt is ₹600 crore and there are 30 crore shares. The SOTP value per share is:
Use the case data. The theoretical ex-rights price of Malabar Textiles is:
hints: This is the simple average of 400 and 300.
The price must adjust down for the discounted issue.
questions.case: Malabar Textiles Ltd has 10 crore shares of face value ₹10 trading at ₹400. It announces a renounceable rights issue of 1 new share for every 4 held at ₹300 per share; the issue is fully subscribed. Six months later it issues a 1:1 bonus on the enlarged capital. Ignore all other market movements.

questions.q: Use the case data. The theoretical value of the rights entitlement needed to subscribe for ONE new share is:
questions.explanation: Value of the right to buy one new share = TERP - issue price = 380 - 300 = ₹80. (Per existing share it is ₹80/4 = ₹20.)
hints: This uses the cum-rights price instead of TERP.
This is the value per existing share, not per new share.
questions.case: Malabar Textiles Ltd has 10 crore shares of face value ₹10 trading at ₹400. It announces a renounceable rights issue of 1 new share for every 4 held at ₹300 per share; the issue is fully subscribed. Six months later it issues a 1:1 bonus on the enlarged capital. Ignore all other market movements.

questions.q: Use the case data. How much money does Malabar raise from the rights issue, and how many shares are outstanding after it?
questions.explanation: New shares = 10 crore / 4 = 2.5 crore; funds = 2.5 crore x ₹300 = ₹750 crore; total shares = 12.5 crore.
hints: This values new shares at the market price of ₹400.
Share count rises after a rights issue.
This treats it as a 1:1 rights issue.

It announces a renounceable rights issue of 1 new share for every 4 held at ₹300 per share; the issue is fully subscribed. Six months later it issues a 1:1 bonus on the enlarged capital. Ignore all other market movements.

questions.q: Use the case data. An investor held 400 shares before the rights issue and subscribed fully to her entitlement. After the bonus, she holds about how many shares and at what theoretical price?
questions.explanation: Rights: 400/4 = 100 new shares → 500 shares at TERP ₹380. 1:1 bonus → 1,000 shares at about ₹190.
hints: The price must halve after a 1:1 bonus.
questions.case: Malabar Textiles Ltd has 10 crore shares of face value ₹10 trading at ₹400. It announces a renounceable rights issue of 1 new share for every 4 held at ₹300 per share; the issue is fully subscribed. Six months later it issues a 1:1 bonus on the enlarged capital. Ignore all other market movements.

questions.q: India, a major exporter of a particular agricultural commodity, suddenly bans its export. The most likely immediate effect is:
options: Domestic prices fall while international prices tend to rise
Domestic and international prices both fall
questions.explanation: An export ban traps supply at home (pushing domestic prices down) and removes a large supplier from world markets (pushing international prices up).
hints: World supply shrinks, so international prices tend to rise.
More supply stays at home, so domestic prices tend to fall.
A major exporter's ban moves both markets.

questions.q: An analyst quietly changes the meaning of 'Buy' from 'expected return above 15% over 12 months' to 'above 5% over 3 years', without telling readers, so that more stocks qualify as Buys. This is:
options: Acceptable, because rating definitions are internal
Acceptable if the target price is unchanged
Contrary to the requirement that ratings, including time horizon and benchmark, be clearly defined and consistently applied
Required to align with market consensus
questions.explanation: Rating definitions must be disclosed and applied consistently; silently changing them misleads readers and breaches the report-quality requirements.
hints: Rating definitions must be disclosed to readers.
The issue is the undisclosed change in rating meaning.

questions.q: Use the case data. Compare the Sharpe ratios of Fund P and the benchmark:
options: P 0.50, benchmark 0.40 - P better on a total-risk basis
questions.explanation: Sharpe P = (15 - 6)/18 = 0.50; benchmark = (12 - 6)/15 = 0.40. P delivers more excess return per unit of total risk.
hints: These divide total return by SD without subtracting Rf.

questions.q: Use the case data. Fund P's Treynor ratio compared with the benchmark's is:
hints: These use total return without subtracting Rf.

questions.q: Use the case data. Fund P's Jensen's alpha is:
questions.explanation: CAPM required return = 6 + 1.2 x (12 - 6) = 13.2%. Alpha = 15 - 13.2 = 1.8%.
hints: This is simply Rp - Rm, ignoring beta.

questions.q: Use the case data. If the benchmark falls 10% next month, the beta-implied expected move in Fund P is about:
questions.explanation: Expected move ≈ beta x market move = 1.2 x (-10%) = -12%.
hints: This divides by beta instead of multiplying.
This uses the standard deviation, not beta.

questions.q: Under the RA Regulations as amended in 2025, which of the following would NOT by itself satisfy the qualification requirement for an individual research analyst?
options: A graduate degree in any discipline plus the relevant NISM certification
A CFA Charter plus the relevant NISM certification
NISM's Post Graduate Programme in Securities Markets (Research Analysis)
A post-graduate degree in finance without any NISM certification
questions.explanation: After the 2025 amendment, qualification routes are: graduation (any discipline) or CFA Charter, each plus NISM certification; or the NISM PG programme (RA track). A finance degree alone, without NISM certification, is insufficient.
hints: Correct - NISM certification is still required.

questions.q: A research entity was a co-manager of a further public offer (FPO). For how many days after the FPO is priced must it refrain from publishing research on the issuer?
questions.explanation: The quiet period is 10 days after pricing for an FPO, versus 40 days for an IPO.
hints: 25 days is for IPO underwriters from the offering date.
30 days is part of the personal-trading blackout.

questions.q: Which statement about SEBI's fee framework for research analysts is correct?
options: The fee cap does not apply to non-individual clients and accredited investors, whose fees are bilaterally negotiated
The ₹1,51,000 cap is per client per month
Advance fees for up to three years are allowed with client consent
Fees may be collected in cash if the client insists
questions.explanation: The fee limit (₹1,51,000 per family per year) and related provisions apply to individual and HUF clients; non-individuals and accredited investors negotiate fees bilaterally. Advance is capped at one year; cash is not permitted.
hints: It is per family per year.
The maximum advance is one year.

questions.q: Within how many days must a research analyst resolve a client grievance under the RA Regulations?
questions.explanation: Grievances are to be redressed within 21 calendar days; unresolved disputes can go to SCORES/ODR mechanisms.

questions.q: A pattern with a flat upper resistance line and a rising lower trendline (higher lows) is a(n):
questions.explanation: An ascending triangle has flat resistance and rising support, showing buyers stepping in at higher prices; an upside breakout is the usual resolution.
hints: A descending triangle has flat support and falling highs.
A symmetrical triangle has both lines converging and is direction-neutral.
A falling wedge has two downward-sloping lines.

questions.q: A stock's 20-day simple moving average is ₹500 and the 20-day standard deviation is ₹15. With standard Bollinger Band settings, the upper and lower bands are:
questions.explanation: Standard bands are 20-period SMA ± 2 standard deviations: 500 ± 30 = ₹530 and ₹470.

questions.q: The MACD line crosses below its signal line while both are above zero. This is generally read as:
options: A bearish signal of weakening upward momentum
questions.explanation: A MACD cross below the signal line is a bearish momentum signal; occurring above zero, it often warns that an uptrend is losing steam.
hints: Crossing below the signal line is bearish.
A golden cross refers to the 50-DMA crossing above the 200-DMA.
Readings above zero do not indicate an oversold market.

questions.q: Consider: (I) A trendline gains significance the more times it is touched without being broken. (II) Once resistance is decisively broken, it tends to act as support. (III) A price channel is formed by drawing a line parallel to the main trendline. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are standard principles: more touches make a trendline more valid; broken resistance becomes support (role reversal); a channel line is drawn parallel to the basic trendline.
hints: II and III are also correct.
